title: fix: nvurisrcbin FPS watchdog restart corrupts vsrc_0 pad, stalling stream 0 permanently
description: The 90s FPS watchdog calls schedule_stream_restart() on nvurisrcbin (stream 0). Cycling nvurisrcbin through NULL does not clean its dynamic vsrc_0 pad, so when it returns to PLAYING GStreamer emits 'Padname vsrc_0 is not unique'. After that, no video pad can be added and stream 0 is permanently stuck at 0fps despite nvurisrcbin's own reconnect still running. Fix: skip the NULL→PLAYING state cycle for nvurisrcbin streams; let built-in reconnect handle drops. Escalate to full service restart (loop.quit) only after 300s.
close_reason: Fixed in commit 3028c2b: track nvurisrcbin streams in gst_builder, skip destructive state-cycle restart for them, escalate to service restart after 300s instead

Stream 0 RTSP drops root cause (confirmed 2026-05-04): gst_builder.py was silently overriding tcp→auto (UDP multi) for nvurisrcbin on stream 0, despite HICON_RTSP_PROTOCOL_0=tcp. UDP has no retransmission so any backpressure/packet loss killed the session. Fix: HICON_STREAM_0_NVURISRCBIN_RESPECT_CONFIGURED_PROTOCOL=true in .env. Confirmed by 3-soak proof (baseline=drops, force-tcp=0 outages in 330s). All the camera-side theories (300s firmware timer, bitrate, audio, CH102 switch) were red herrings — the bug was in our own code.

Inference recording (HICON_ENABLE_INFERENCE_VIDEO=true) on the pyrometer stream (Stream 1) breaks its nvinfer branch: the recording tee triggers 'nvvideoconvert buffer transform failed' -> 'pgie-pyrometer: Internal data stream error (-5)', pyrometer inference gets paused and Stream 1 drops to 0 fps while Streams 0/2 stay healthy. Camera (192.168.27.253) and RTSP feed are fine (pings, ffprobe HEVC 1280x720@25). Fix: disable recording on Stream 1 via HICON_ENABLE_INFERENCE_VIDEO_STREAM_1=false (or globally). Pouring cameras 0/2 record fine. Confirmed 2026-06-09.

CORRECTED 2026-06-12: The '300s irreducible camera hardware cycle' conclusion was WRONG. Actual root cause: camera 0's default gateway was set to 192.168.28.1 which DOES NOT EXIST on the network (ARP incomplete forever). Hikvision firmware's periodic gateway health check failed every cycle and its recovery action bounced the camera's network/streaming stack every ~298.5s (free-running timer), silently killing all RTSP sessions (later RST win0 = TCP state lost), with 0-9s ICMP/HTTP blip. Camera OS never rebooted (uptime 5.6d). Controls: identical cameras 1&2 (same model/firmware) point at gateway 192.168.27.1 which EXISTS and never cycled. Also explains why replacing CP Plus with Hikvision didn't help (same dead gateway on 28.x). The old '95s TCP refusal' no longer applied by June (new TCP accepted within seconds). FIX (2026-06-12 19:09): gateway changed to 192.168.28.8 (NVR-1, always-on, answers ARP) via ISAPI PUT + camera reboot. Verification: watch [RTSP-OUTAGE] in pipeline.log for 30+ min.

rtspsrc path for stream 0 (HICON_USE_NVURISRCBIN_0=false) crashes with pgie-pouring: not-negotiated when first frame arrives from camera (~1.3s after PLAYING). Root cause: nvtracker rejects dynamic CAPS event during PLAYING state — caps on pgie_pouring→tracker_0 link aren't pre-established before data flows, unlike nvurisrcbin where vsrc_0 pad connects during PAUSED→PLAYING. Confirmed by: bypass tracker → no crash. Attempted fixes that failed: (1) deep-element-added to set do-rtsp-keep-alive on internal src element (ignored by nvurisrcbin), (2) batched-push-timeout=30s (irrelevant, crash is on first real frame not empty batch), (3) capsfilter(NV12+1600x900) between pgie and tracker (breaks displayq0→nvosd_0 link), (4) capsfilter(NV12 only) between pgie and tracker (same link failure). Next approach: use nvvideoconvert between caps0 and premuxq0 to output RGBA and match standard DeepStream sample pipeline topology, OR send RECONFIGURE event on tracker sink pad after PLAYING.
